title: Alpha CRDs are still served — 0.34 will not read them
quote: `0.33.0`+ _only_ supports Karpenter v1beta1 APIs and will not work with existing Provisioner, AWSNodeTemplate or Machine alpha APIs. Do not upgrade to `0.34.0`+ without first upgrading to `0.32.x`. This version supports both the alpha and beta APIs, allowing you to migrate all of your existing APIs to beta APIs without experiencing downtime.
remediation: Upgrade to 0.32.x first and migrate every alpha object to the v1beta1 APIs before coming here.
verifyCommand: kubectl get crd -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.group | test("karpenter")) | "\(.metadata.name) served=\([.spec.versions[] | select(.served) | .name] | join(","))"'  # each Karpenter CRD and the API versions it still serves

title: An EC2NodeClass using the Ubuntu AMI family cannot create nodes on 1.29+
quote: The Ubuntu EKS optimized AMI has moved from 20.04 to 22.04 for Kubernetes 1.29+. This new AMI version is __not currently__ supported for users relying on AMI auto-discovery with the Ubuntu AMI family. More details can be found in this GitHub issue. Please review this issue before upgrading to Kubernetes 1.29 if you are using the Ubuntu AMI family. Upgrading to 1.29 without making any changes to your EC2NodeClass will result in Karpenter being unable to create new nodes.
remediation: Pin the AMI explicitly with `amiSelectorTerms` before taking this cluster to Kubernetes 1.29. Ubuntu AMI auto-discovery does not cover the 22.04 image that 1.29 requires, so Karpenter is left unable to create new nodes — on a cluster that scales with Karpenter, that is an outage waiting for the first scale-up.
verifyCommand: kubectl get ec2nodeclasses -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[]? | select(.spec.amiFamily == "Ubuntu") | "\(.metadata.name) amiSelectorTerms=\((.spec.amiSelectorTerms // []) | length)"'  # a row with 0 selector terms relies on the auto-discovery that is broken for Ubuntu on 1.29

title: Re-enabled webhooks need ports 8000, 8001, 8081 and 8443 reachable

detection.reason: whether a NetworkPolicy actually blocks these ports for the Karpenter pods depends on the policy's selectors and rules, which are not part of the collected projection

quote: Webhooks have been re-enabled by default starting in `0.34.9` to faciliate migration to `v1.0`. If your cluster has network policies that block Ingress then ports `8000`, `8001`, `8081`, `8443` will need to be allowlisted. You may still choose to disable webhooks through the helm chart.
remediation: Karpenter re-enables its webhooks from 0.34.9. Allowlist ports 8000, 8001, 8081 and 8443 for the Karpenter namespace in any NetworkPolicy that restricts ingress.
verifyCommand: kubectl get networkpolicy -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name) types=\((.spec.policyTypes // []) | join(","))"'  # check any policy in the Karpenter namespace against ports 8000, 8001, 8081 and 8443

title: The NodePool CRD has to be updated before 0.34 can accept budgets

detection.reason: the CRD's schema fields are not collected — only each CRD's name, group and served version names are, so whether this NodePool CRD already knows about budgets cannot be read

quote: Karpenter now supports `nodepool.spec.disruption.budgets`, which allows users to control the speed of disruption in the cluster. Since this requires an update to the Custom Resource, before upgrading, you should re-apply the new updates to the CRDs. Check out Disruption Budgets for more.
remediation: Re-apply the Karpenter CRDs before upgrading. `nodepool.spec.disruption.budgets` is a new field and Helm never updates CRDs on an upgrade, so on an un-updated CRD the API server strips the budgets you write — leaving disruption unbounded while the manifest says otherwise.
verifyCommand: kubectl get crd -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.group | test("karpenter")) | "\(.metadata.name) served=\([.spec.versions[] | select(.served) | .name] | join(","))"'  # each Karpenter CRD and the API versions it still serves

title: A NodePool without budgets gets the new 10% disruption default

detection.reason: the NodePool CRD DEFAULTS spec.disruption.budgets to [{nodes: 10%}] in both its v1 and v1beta1 schemas, so every NodePool the API server returns carries the field whatever the operator wrote. Presence therefore cannot separate 'budgets were set' from 'the default was filled in', and a rule keyed on it would read CLEARED on every cluster (verified against a live v1.0.5 CRD on 2026-09-07)

quote: With Disruption Budgets, Karpenter will disrupt multiple batches of nodes simultaneously, which can result in overall quicker scale-down of your cluster. Before `0.34.0`, Karpenter had a hard-coded parallelism limit for each type of disruption. In `0.34.0`+, Karpenter will now disrupt at most 10% of nodes for a given NodePool. There is no setting that will be perfectly equivalent with the behavior prior to `0.34.0`. When considering how to configure your budgets, please refer to the following limits for versions prior to `0.34.0`:
remediation: These NodePools declare no disruption budgets, so from 0.34 they take the new default of at most 10% of their nodes disrupted at once. That is a behaviour change in both directions: faster than the old one-node-at-a-time limit for non-empty consolidation, slower than the old unlimited parallelism for empty nodes. Set `spec.disruption.budgets` explicitly if either matters to you.
verifyCommand: kubectl get nodepools -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[]? | "\(.metadata.name) budgets=\((.spec.disruption.budgets // []) | tostring)"'  # a NodePool showing exactly [{"nodes":"10%"}] is on the CRD default, which is what 0.34 changes to; anything else was set deliberately and is unaffected

title: Karpenter's own resource requests may no longer be enough

detection.reason: how much headroom a controller's current limits leave depends on live usage, which is not part of an inventory snapshot

quote: To support Disruption Budgets, `0.34.0`+ includes critical changes to Karpenter's core controllers, which allows Karpenter to consider multiple batches of disrupting nodes simultaneously. This increases Karpenter's performance with the potential downside of higher CPU and memory utilization from the Karpenter pod. While the magnitude of this difference varies on a case-by-case basis, when upgrading to Karpenter `0.34.0`+, please note that you may need to increase the resources allocated to the Karpenter controller pods.
remediation: Review the CPU and memory allocated to the Karpenter controller pods before upgrading. 0.34 considers several batches of disrupting nodes at once, which costs more of both — a limit that was comfortable can become an OOMKill on a large cluster.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy,daemonset -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.template.spec.containers[]?.image? // "" | test("karpenter/controller")) | "\(.kind)/\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name) \(.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image)"'  # the Karpenter controller workload and the exact version tag it runs -- then read its resources block

title: A default podSecurityContext with fsGroup 65536 is added

detection.reason: whether a sidecar tolerates an fsGroup depends on what its image expects of the volumes it mounts, which no inventory can answer

quote: Karpenter now adds a default `podSecurityContext` that configures the `fsgroup: 65536` of volumes in the pod. If you are using sidecar containers, you should review if this configuration is compatible for them. You can disable this default `podSecurityContext` through helm by performing `--set podSecurityContext=null` when installing/upgrading the chart.
remediation: If you run sidecars alongside Karpenter, check they work with `fsgroup: 65536` applied to the pod's volumes. The default can be removed with `--set podSecurityContext=null`.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy,daemonset -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.template.spec.containers[]?.image? // "" | test("karpenter/controller")) | "\(.kind)/\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name) \(.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image)"'  # the Karpenter controller workload and the exact version tag it runs -- then read the pod securityContext and each sidecar's volume mounts

title: Karpenter starts resolving DNS through the cluster's own service

detection.reason: the failure mode is a runtime dependency (Karpenter resolving through in-cluster DNS that may itself need Karpenter to schedule), not a field on any collected object

quote: The `dnsPolicy` for the Karpenter controller pod has been changed back to the Kubernetes cluster default of `ClusterFirst`. Setting our `dnsPolicy` to `Default` (confusingly, this is not the Kubernetes cluster default) caused more confusion for any users running IPv6 clusters with dual-stack nodes or anyone running Karpenter with dependencies on cluster services (like clusters running service meshes). This change may be breaking for any users on Fargate or MNG who were allowing Karpenter to manage their in-cluster DNS service (`core-dns` on most clusters). If you still want the old behavior here, you can change the `dnsPolicy` to point to use `Default` by setting the helm value on install/upgrade with `--set dnsPolicy=Default`. More details on this issue can be found in the following Github issues: #2186 and #4947.
remediation: This is breaking if Karpenter manages the capacity your in-cluster DNS runs on — on Fargate or a managed node group, `ClusterFirst` makes Karpenter depend on a service it may be responsible for scheduling. Set `--set dnsPolicy=Default` to keep the old behaviour.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy,daemonset -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.template.spec.containers[]?.image? // "" | test("karpenter/controller")) | "\(.kind)/\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name) \(.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image)"'  # the Karpenter controller workload and the exact version tag it runs -- then read its dnsPolicy

title: A NodePool that sets template resources stops accepting edits

detection.reason: reads the presence flag the agent writes for every NodePool; the resources map itself is never collected

quote: Karpenter now disallows `nodepool.spec.template.spec.resources` to be set. The webhook validation never allowed `nodepool.spec.template.spec.resources`. We are now ensuring that CEL validation also disallows `nodepool.spec.template.spec.resources` to be set. If you were previously setting the resources field on your NodePool, ensure that you remove this field before upgrading to the newest version of Karpenter or else updates to the resource may fail on the new version.
remediation: Remove `spec.template.spec.resources` from these NodePools before upgrading. CEL validation starts rejecting the field, so any later update to one of these objects fails — including the update you make to fix it under pressure.
verifyCommand: kubectl get nodepools -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[]? | select(.spec.template.spec.resources != null) | .metadata.name'  # each NodePool printed sets a field that CEL validation refuses from 0.34
